title: New Drug Modalities 2026
gist: BCG's 2026 New Drug Modalities report finds new-modality forward pipeline value flat at $198B (57% of a $347B total) as conventional drugs rebound on obesity; antibodies mature, gene editing, RNAi and radiopharma grow, cell therapy lags, and China-sourced assets reach ~50% of big-pharma modality deal value.

insights.claim: Total five-year forward biopharma pipeline value rose to $347B in 2026 from $330B, but new modalities fell to 57% of it from 60% as conventional therapies recovered to 43%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The modality premium is eroding; conventional small molecules deserve renewed weight in biopharma allocation.
insights.locator: A Plateau in New-Modality Pipeline Value

insights.claim: New-modality forward pipeline value held flat at $198B because roughly $40B of growth was offset by downward forecast revisions, the largest being CagriSema after Redefine 1 weight loss undershot expectations.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Trial disappointments in a single heavyweight asset can stall an entire category's aggregate value.
insights.locator: The value of the new-modality pipeline, meanwhile, held steady

insights.claim: The conventional-therapy pipeline grew about $18B, its strongest growth in the analysis's history, driven by small-molecule obesity, oncology, cardiovascular and rare-disease products.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Oral metabolic drugs are the main force pulling value back to conventional modalities.
insights.locator: The value of the conventional-therapy pipeline grew

insights.claim: Analysts expect seven of the top ten 2031 products to be new modalities versus nine projected last year for 2030, with Foundayo and Rinvoq entering and Keytruda and Wegovy dropping out on loss of exclusivity and IRA pricing exposure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Patent cliffs and Inflation Reduction Act pricing are reshaping the top-product league table beyond 2030.
insights.locator: The five-year outlook has also shifted

insights.claim: Mounjaro rose to the top-selling product ranking, Zepbound moved from tenth to fifth with nearly doubled projected revenue, and Skyrizi rose from fifth to third.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Lilly's incretin franchise and AbbVie's Skyrizi are the commercial winners in the 2026 rankings.
insights.locator: Mounjaro rose from third to the top position

insights.claim: Antibodies are maturing rather than stagnating: marketed monoclonal antibody forward value grew $24B while pipeline value shrank, which BCG reads as commercial maturation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Antibody value is migrating from pipeline to revenue, favouring commercial-stage holders.
insights.locator: Monoclonal Antibodies

insights.claim: Chinese and South Korean companies dominate ADC pipeline expansion: 17 of the 25 firms with the largest increase in ADC pipeline size are Chinese and four are South Korean, with LigaChem growing from 15 to 35 products.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Asian developers are now the main source of ADC innovation that Western pharma will license or buy.
insights.locator: Antibody-Drug Conjugates

insights.claim: Summit Therapeutics and Akeso's ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific filed with the FDA in January 2026, is the largest single driver of multispecific antibody value, which is flat at about $6B in forward pipeline value.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Ivonescimab approval is the key catalyst for the multispecific category.
insights.locator: Multispecific Antibodies

insights.claim: GLP-1 products make up roughly half the projected value of recombinant proteins but a small fraction of product count, and their aggregate forecast value fell 7% on CagriSema's revision, semaglutide IRA and LOE exposure, and oral GLP-1 competition.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Obesity-drug value is concentrated and being compressed by pricing, competition and exclusivity loss even as indications broaden.
insights.locator: The decline was driven by three factors

insights.claim: Non-GLP-1 recombinant proteins grew 9% in count and 22% in forward value, largely in immunoglobulin products, showing protein growth beyond obesity.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Diversified protein exposure outside GLP-1 is growing faster than the headline obesity trade.
insights.locator: Non-GLP-1 recombinant products, by contrast

insights.claim: CAR-T gained validation (Gilead/Arcellx anito-cel BLA accepted February 2026) while clinical-phase pipeline value fell because small developers face financing and prioritization pressure, as with Caribou's 2025 workforce reduction.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Clinical wins are not translating into financing for small cell-therapy developers, so consolidation and distress are likely.
insights.locator: CAR-T.

insights.claim: TCR-T, CAR-NK, TIL and stem cell forward value together has stayed relatively flat since BCG began tracking in 2020; TIL value is almost entirely Iovance's Amtagvi, constrained by manufacturing complexity and cost.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Emerging cell modalities have not scaled commercially in six years; treat them as single-asset binary bets.
insights.locator: These emerging cell therapy modalities continued to show stagnant

insights.claim: Gene editing grew at a 21% CAGR in forward value, and Intellia's lonvo-z (rolling BLA from April 2026 for hereditary angioedema) would be the first in vivo CRISPR therapy on the market if approved.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Lonvo-z approval is a watershed catalyst for the editing sector, with Beam's base editors holding the highest clinical-phase revenue forecasts.
insights.locator: Gene editing is among the fastest-growing modalities

insights.claim: Gene augmentation plateaued as Elevidys' forecasted marketed value fell after a 2025 safety hold and label restrictions, offsetting growth in clinical-phase assets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Safety events on a lead gene-therapy product depress the whole modality's forecasts.
insights.locator: Gene augmentation saw clinical-phase forward pipeline value

insights.claim: RNAi forward marketed value rose from $11.5B to $16.9B, driven chiefly by Alnylam's Amvuttra gaining an ATTR cardiomyopathy label beyond polyneuropathy.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Label expansions convert platform promise into revenue; Alnylam is the clearest example.
insights.locator: RNAi: RNAi forward pipeline value was nearly flat

insights.claim: DNA and RNA therapies grew Phase 3 product counts by roughly two-thirds in a year, driven by Western pure-plays, large-pharma platforms and Chinese biotechs, while mRNA pipeline and marketed value kept contracting post-pandemic.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Nucleic-acid growth is rotating away from mRNA toward oligonucleotide and RNAi platforms.
insights.locator: Nucleic Acids: Growing Pipelines Beyond mRNA

insights.claim: mRNA shows pockets of momentum despite contraction: Moderna's mFlusiva is the first approved mRNA seasonal flu vaccine and Merck/Moderna's intismeran is the first mRNA cancer vaccine with positive Phase 3 melanoma results.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Oncology and flu approvals are the potential recovery catalysts for mRNA.
insights.locator: However, there has been positive momentum

insights.claim: Radiopharmaceuticals, newly tracked, posted the highest product-count CAGR of any modality, with Novartis' Pluvicto expanding earlier in prostate cancer and FDA decisions in H2 2026 for ITM-11 (Lu-177) and Convergent's Conv01-α (Ac-225).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Alpha-emitter approvals in H2 2026 are near-term catalysts for the next radioligand wave.
insights.locator: Radiopharmaceuticals: Quickly Expanding

insights.claim: The top 20 biopharma companies spent roughly $290B on new-modality deals from 2023 through 2026 YTD, including $127B across 50 deals from H2 2025 to May 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sustained big-pharma deal demand underpins valuations of validated new-modality assets.
insights.locator: Antibodies and China-Originated Assets Anchor Deal Activity

insights.claim: China-originated assets were about 50% of top-20 biopharma 2026 YTD new-modality deal value, up from 40% the prior year.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Chinese biotech is becoming the primary external innovation source for Western pharma.
insights.locator: China remains a primary source of licensed assets

insights.claim: Large 2026 acquisitions cluster at clinical or commercial validation, including AbbVie–Apogee ($10.9B), Gilead–Arcellx ($7.8B), Lilly–Centessa ($7.8B), plus Novartis–Avidity ($12B), signalling a premium for de-risked late-stage assets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Buyers pay up after clinical inflection, so the value-capture point for small caps is data readout.
insights.locator: Late-stage M&A commands a premium

insights.claim: Cell and gene therapy is overwhelmingly a small-cap phenomenon (about 35 focused companies under $1B, only 5 above $5B), and acquisitions tend to close at the $1B–$5B clinical-inflection tier, as with Gilead–Arcellx, Lilly–Verve and BMS–Orbital.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The $1B–$5B market-cap tier with a Phase 3 lead asset is the highest-probability M&A target zone.
insights.locator: Beyond antibodies and proteins and peptides

insights.claim: New-modality companies follow a maturation arc by market cap: below $1B typically a single asset (median ~100% of 2031 value from one product), $1B–$5B a Phase 3 lead, $5B–$20B a marketed lead with multi-modality pipelines, and above $20B broad marketed franchises with argenx and Alnylam the exceptions anchored on new modalities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Use the tier model to judge concentration risk and where scaling requires clinical progression versus modality breadth.
insights.locator: The third tier, $5 billion to $20 billion, marks an inflection point
